reviews.review:
Mass Effect 3 is a game that fights your sense of good taste in storytelling all the way through (and your patience trying to play the game), despite offering up what is arguably the best gameplay in the trilogy.

I have played this game three times through, with two 100% playthroughs on Origin. I own four copies of this game, including several digital versions, on Origin, and I still have to struggle through performance problems and slowdown every time I play the game. (There are pirated copies of this game that have better performance/better DLC integration than the official version -- let that sink in for a moment.) 

EA's presentation of this game smacks of something that was pushed out in a day to capitalize on the publisher's (re)launch on Steam. The DLC bundle page advertises extra collector's edition content and a DLC (From Ashes) that's already included in this "deluxe" edition of the product. The game shipped with a UI/registration problem with Origin that's inexplicably as bad as it was at launch, with no reason or support given to customers and interest being pushed towards the "Legendary Edition" remaster that's planned to come out at some point next year. The framerate consistently drops, resulting in players having to resort to a hotfix to address the issue. That shouldn't be a surprise, though -- witness the years-long debacle regarding "Bioware Points", the system that originally pushed EA off Steam in the first place, precisely because they couldn't control an internal economy within their flagship titles years before in-app purchases became a thing.

What's most surprising to me is that this sequel and its DLC is that it was pushed out suddenly by EA... but all of ME2's DLC is still missing in action. There are numerous small events, scenarios and bonuses in the third game that only work/appear if you played a savefile routed through the second game, and short of grabbing a pre-made save from a site like MassEffect2Saves, there's been no answer or support from EA over the matter. Everyone loved Lair of the Shadow Broker, and yet, you'll never see any of the extra content that mission brings you in the third game (including additional romance content with Liara, bonuses for Shepard and some unique conversations) if you didn't resort to third-party help to fix it.

As far as the game itself goes, there is only one way to play -- with mods. Seriously, mods like the Expanded Galaxy Mod, Orikon25's Priority: Earth Overhaul Mod, Kinkojiro's Ark Mod and the Bonus Power Packs took what was a middling sequel and turned it into one of the best RPGs of this generation -- largely by rebalancing galactic exploration and decision-making to actually make the player feel like they're playing a decisive role in the Reaper War. If you are going to pursue this franchise, either invest in the time to install those mods or avoid this entirely, because if you are playing unmodded, there's a lot you have to work through to get to the great moments.

The gameplay hits a sweet spot between the overt "classic" Bioware RPG combat of the first game and the overly simplified "arcade-y" shooting gallery of the second. You'll have plenty of thrilling moments launching off strings of power combos alongside your squadmates, facing off against some interesting variants of Reapers, the Geth, Cerberus and other forces, and finding new armor and weapons in varied locales.

The story, meanwhile, is a step down from the first game, and not much of a speck on 2, either. Everyone runs to the meme line of "everything was great until the end," but 3 has plot holes the size of a Mack truck that will hit the player at full speed. Cerberus goes from a shadowy clandestine organization to a galactic superpower with unlimited resources in the span of six months, with no explanation beyond "shell companies, lol". The collective IQ of characters who should really know better plummets like a rock, and even established anti-villains like Udina and The Illusive Man do really dumb things to motivate the plot. Sidequests, particularly on the Citadel, are laughably short and nothing more than fetch quests. The Crucible is a glorified deus ex machina that's never adequately explained, and you just send personnel and materials without knowing precisely what it does (revealed to be blue/green/red space magic). The (unmodded) final missions mix bland, uninteresting horde modes with bugs galore, questionable character motivations and a final setpiece that lives on in infamy for how tonally inconsistent and illogical it is with the rest of the game -- and the franchise.

Still, there are high points -- several of the squadmates/supporting characters are consistent and have payoffs to the arc they've been cultivating across three games. The game does manage to genuinely pull at your heartstrings at points, with conclusions to character arcs bringing together numerous separate plot threads. Level design and the RPG-type upgrades you can find throughout the game are great, though the War Asset system was an illogical "reward" system that was thankfully addressed through mods.

In the end, if you're going to buy this game, get it to conclude the rest of the trilogy. Don't buy it and play without first running through the prior two games, nor buy it if you're expecting a game that will match the quality of the previous games. The performance issues will continue to be a sticking point, and it is highly likely that EA will discontinue support for this version/push players to the Remastered version, leaving the bugs and latent problems introduced here unsolved.

First off let me say how I am pleased this game does not contain game breaking bugs like the 1st and 2nd titles on origin/steam. (well except for, if you are near Bailey's office, you round the corner at the dead end, and stand next to the atm, eventually a Turian with red features will walk over and box you in between the atm and another person/atm, with no where to go ^_^). Anyways, I am just now experiencing the whole series for the first time and I love that this game continues the lore of the reapers. It seems to lack that powerful feeling of impending danger like Mass Effect 2 did. The combat is improved, you can now dodge although it's useless against regular gun fire as the NPC auto aim is 100 percent dead on to hit you. The missles and other heavy projectiles are when you can dodge and roll. The team is a lot smaller now, only a few people. I really enjoyed it and if you have made it to mass effect 2 and are currently enjoying it, YOU HAVE to continue with the third iteration, you will not regret it. Get the DLC and play The Citadel, by far the best part of the entire game.
Great memories. Gets you hyped for the remastered edition
Superb ending to one of the great gaming trilogies. Runs fine without any issues.
Great story - made me care about it. What more player may want from singleplayer game?

This was a great game until I was linked to EA Play and Steam. Now it hardly ever launches correctly. Steam will not support it  and EA just blames Steam. Love the game. Hate the software companies ability to get their ♥♥♥♥ together.

For those of you who have completed the previous 2 titles in the series this is a must buy ! The story is amazing and choices that you had made in the previous 2 games (and the choices you will make in this one) do make an impact on how the story progresses and ultimately how the game ends. Combat is decent, nothing amazing about it but it is a noticeable upgrade over ME2's combat. All in all a satisfying conclusion to the trilogy.

Now for those who haven't completed (or played) the previous 2 games, honestly it is a tough sell since the story is to some extent linked and carried forward from the previous 2 games. The characters along with their backgrounds and the universe itself are quite complex and combat alone is not enough to make it worth your while. I would sincerely recommend playing the previous games first before starting this one.
